waterfall_rules.order: classes by the analyst's rank number, lowest first; classes of one rank share pro rata; the secured_debt class must rank strictly first
waterfall_rules.distributable: enterprise value only (EBITDA x multiple); cash is not added, costs are not deducted
waterfall_rules.recipe: paid = min(available, group total); recovery = paid / group total (one division, 38 digits half-even); when paid = group total each distribution is its claim; when 0 < paid < group total the distributions are allocated by exact largest remainder at the rank quantum q = 10^(paid.adjusted() - 37), ties to the later class in claims order, and sum to paid exactly (rulings round 8 A-1); shortfall = claim - distribution (38 digits); next available = available - paid; equity residual = what remains (a known 0 when creditors absorb all value); T4E.9 balances exactly
waterfall_rules.missing: a missing claim blocks its rank group and every lower rank and the equity residual; a missing or unassessed EV blocks everything; a known EV of 0 gives known 0 recoveries; nothing becomes 0
waterfall_rules.value_break: the first rank group whose paid < total; if none, equity; not determinable (missing with the root reason) when an earlier group is blocked
waterfall_rules.attachment: claims ahead / EBITDA and claims through the class / EBITDA (the multiple at which the class is covered in full); missing when EBITDA is missing, zero or negative
waterfall_rules.plan_fit: creditor: Paid in full <=> recovery 1; Receives reorganised equity <=> 0 < recovery < 1; No recovery <=> recovery 0; Not determined <=> recovery missing. Equity: Equity retained <=> residual > 0; No recovery <=> residual 0; Not determined <=> residual missing

property_tests.conservation: for every case with all inputs known: sum of creditor distributions + equity residual = enterprise value exactly (T4E.9 balance = 0)
property_tests.priority: no class receives value while a better-ranked class has a shortfall; recoveries are non-decreasing in enterprise value
property_tests.pari_passu: classes of one rank have equal recovery
property_tests.break_monotone: as the multiple rises the value break moves to the same or a more junior rank
property_tests.missing_never_zero: removing a claim amount or the multiple never produces a known 0

own_limitations: Multiples, claim ranks and plan treatment are analyst assumptions without a source citation; no market or restructuring-plan source is an input.
Value available to claims is the enterprise value only: balance-sheet cash is not added and restructuring, administrative and financing costs are not deducted unless a claim class states them.

The waterfall applies strict priority by the analyst's rank number; classes of one rank share pro rata. Collateral value, guarantees, structural subordination and intercreditor terms are not modelled.

Claims are the 31 December 2025 balances: accrued interest, fees, make-whole amounts, lease and pension claims, contingent and rejection-damage claims are not stated in any source and are not modelled; they are not zero.
New-money or priming debt is not modelled: the legal source requires the consent of every lender for additional debt, so no debt-in-possession financing is assumed.
Enterprise value is the analyst's multiple applied to a CP-2G forecast EBITDA that rests on analyst-assumed drivers; it is not a market or court valuation.
The fulcrum is the first rank whose recovery is below its claim; the analyst's named fulcrum is checked against it. Plan treatment is checked for fit with the recovery, not for legal feasibility.
Recoveries are not probability-weighted and the valuations are not scenarios of equal likelihood.

own_limitations: Multiples, claim ranks and plan treatment are analyst assumptions without a source citation; no market or restructuring-plan source is an input.
Value available to claims is the enterprise value only: balance-sheet cash is not added and restructuring, administrative and financing costs are not deducted unless a claim class states them.

The waterfall applies strict priority by the analyst's rank number; classes of one rank share pro rata. Collateral value, guarantees, structural subordination and intercreditor terms are not modelled.

Claims are the 31 December 2025 balances: accrued interest, fees, make-whole amounts, lease and pension claims, contingent and rejection-damage claims are not stated in any source and are not modelled; they are not zero.
New-money or priming debt is not modelled: the legal source requires the consent of every lender for additional debt, so no debt-in-possession financing is assumed.
Enterprise value is the analyst's multiple applied to a CP-2G forecast EBITDA that rests on analyst-assumed drivers; it is not a market or court valuation.
The fulcrum is the first rank whose recovery is below its claim; the analyst's named fulcrum is checked against it. Plan treatment is checked for fit with the recovery, not for legal feasibility.
Recoveries are not probability-weighted and the valuations are not scenarios of equal likelihood.
CP-3C (refinancing and liability management) is an optional input that this version never reads.
The lender protection rating is read from CP-4 and stays Insufficient Information: security, guarantee, default, cure and voting terms are not supplied.

own_limitations: Multiples, claim ranks and plan treatment are analyst assumptions without a source citation; no market or restructuring-plan source is an input.
Value available to claims is the enterprise value only: balance-sheet cash is not added and restructuring, administrative and financing costs are not deducted unless a claim class states them.

The waterfall applies strict priority by the analyst's rank number; classes of one rank share pro rata. Collateral value, guarantees, structural subordination and intercreditor terms are not modelled.

Claims are the 31 December 2025 balances: accrued interest, fees, make-whole amounts, lease and pension claims, contingent and rejection-damage claims are not stated in any source and are not modelled; they are not zero.
New-money or priming debt is not modelled: the legal source requires the consent of every lender for additional debt, so no debt-in-possession financing is assumed.
Enterprise value is the analyst's multiple applied to a CP-2G forecast EBITDA that rests on analyst-assumed drivers; it is not a market or court valuation.
The fulcrum is the first rank whose recovery is below its claim; the analyst's named fulcrum is checked against it. Plan treatment is checked for fit with the recovery, not for legal feasibility.
Recoveries are not probability-weighted and the valuations are not scenarios of equal likelihood.
CP-3C (refinancing and liability management) is an optional input that this version never reads.
The lender protection rating is read from CP-4 and stays Insufficient Information: security, guarantee, default, cure and voting terms are not supplied.
The claim of Senior secured term loan is not available: total debt is missing in CP-1 for LTM Q4 25: 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31; every recovery at or below its rank is Not calculable.
The fulcrum of the base valuation cannot be determined, so the analyst names none.

The fulcrum of the stress valuation cannot be determined, so the analyst names none.

tamper.why_this_fact: the table cell holds only the fact id and the step output holds the submission, so the value-break text lives only in the result Module; cp4c.probe rebuilds it from the journaled payload and the bound heads (stress valuation breaks at the term loan)
recipe: 1. Copy the closed positive store directory (blobs, snapshots, current, audit) to a scratch path.
2. Load the CP-4C head's result Module; replace only the text of fact T4E.7.v03.value_break (its shown spelling is that text); every other fact, table, claim and limitation unchanged.
3. Serialise the forged Module as Execution._store does (model_dump_json); its sha256 R2 equals Module.content_hash(); write blobs/R2.

4. Build a new ExecutionSnapshot equal to the current one with the CP-4C Attempt.result_sha256 and Head.result_sha256 set to R2 and the same parent; write snapshots/<its sha256>.json and rewrite current.

5. In the retained receipt: set the CP-4C SettledHead.result_sha256 to R2; set receipt.snapshot_sha256 and the CP-4C settling OwnerSubmission.snapshot_after_sha256 to the new digest (record re-retained under its new content hash, the old record deleted); rewrite audit/receipt.sha256 with the forged receipt's content_hash.

expect.passes: everything upstream of the probe: audit inventory, blob and snapshot hashes, ancestor walk, head_of equality, begin and publication records, call and read replay, journaled-step replay
expect.refuses: cp4c.probe raises WorkflowError('identity_mismatch'); verify_owner_run_receipt raises identity_mismatch
expect.test_asserts: _verify_audit and every check before _PROBES pass on the forged copy; then cp4c.probe raises identity_mismatch (asserting identity_mismatch alone would not show the probe was reached)
